lines: I remember being stitched back into myself. Your hands held the thread.
The cure left scars, but good leather can carry scars. So can I.
You stayed close when I was dangerous. I will not forget that.
My hands remembered the awl before my mind remembered the room.
The smell of the tannery was the first thing that felt like home.
I woke afraid of everyone except you.
Each morning brings another small piece of myself back.
I can work again. I did not know how much I would miss it.
You gave me time I was certain I had lost.
I remember your voice cutting through the fever.
The village looks ordinary again, and I am grateful for that.
I found my old apron yesterday. Holding it made me cry.
Some memories are still gone, but the fear is fading.
I owe you more than a pair of boots could ever repay.
Thank you for seeing a neighbor when I looked like a monster.
I slept through the night without waking in panic.
The children no longer run when they see me. That helps.
I am learning not to flinch at every sudden sound.
Being alive feels strange, but it feels good.
If you ever need shelter or sturdy gear, come to me.
Your face is worn into the memory, but the edges are rough.
I remember straps, shaking, and a second chance pulled tight.
You helped me, did you not? I know that much.
My mind keeps placing you in rooms where you were never standing.
I recognize your voice more clearly than your face.
Was it night when you brought the cure? The memory keeps changing.
I found my tools, but I could not remember where I kept them.
The village bell sounds familiar and frightening at once.
I know this workshop belongs to me. It still feels borrowed.
People tell me I am safe now. I am trying to believe them.
Did I speak to you after the fever broke?
My hands can stitch a straight seam even when my thoughts wander.
Some names return when I smell the dye vats.
I remember being cold, then waking under a blanket.
Please forgive me if I ask the same thing twice.
There are days missing from my memory altogether.
I keep expecting the hunger to come back.
You look kind in the pieces I can recall.
I may not remember every detail, but I know you saved me.
Stay a moment. Familiar company helps the room settle.
I remember you, and I remember the tearing. Both are true.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure worked, but I need you to give me room.
Your voice brings back parts of that night I would rather lose.
I am grateful, even if I cannot stand close to you yet.
Please do not reach for me without warning.
My mind knows I am safe. My body has not learned it.
I remember your face above me when I could not move.
You did the right thing. That does not make the memory gentle.
I need time before this feels like a rescue instead of another attack.
The workshop helps. Everything here stays where I expect it.
I still wake with my hands clenched around the blanket.
Do not mistake my fear for ingratitude.
Some days I can speak about it. Today is not one of them.
I trust what the others told me, but the panic comes first.
Let me keep the door open while we talk.
I know your hands carried the cure. I also remember fighting them.
The smell of leather brings me back when my thoughts slip.
I will thank you properly when I can do it without shaking.
For now, knowing you came back is enough.
